text: The Eiffel Tower is a wrought-iron lattice tower on the Champ de Mars in Paris, France.
lines:
0	The Eiffel Tower is a wrought-iron lattice tower on the Champ de Mars in Paris, France.
1	It is named after the engineer Gustave Eiffel, whose company designed and built the tower from 1887 to 1889.
2	Constructed as the centerpiece of the 1889 World's Fair, it was initially criticized by some of France's leading artists and intellectuals for its design.
3	The Eiffel Tower is located in the 7th arrondissement of Paris, situated on the south bank of the Seine river.
4	It is the most-visited paid monument in the world, with 6.91 million visitors in 2015.
5	The tower is 330 metres tall, about the same height as an 81-storey building, and the tallest structure in Paris.

text: London is the capital and largest city of England and the United Kingdom.
lines:
0	London is the capital and largest city of England and the United Kingdom, with a population of just under 10 million people.
1	It stands on the River Thames in south-east England at the head of a 50-mile estuary down to the North Sea.
2	London contains four World Heritage Sites: the Tower of London, Kew Gardens, the Palace of Westminster along with Westminster Abbey, and the historic settlement of Greenwich.
3	Other notable landmarks include Buckingham Palace, the London Eye, Piccadilly Circus, St Paul's Cathedral, Tower Bridge, and Trafalgar Square.
4	London does not contain the Eiffel Tower, which is located in Paris, France.

text: Paris is the capital and most populous city of France.
lines:
0	Paris is the capital and most populous city of France, with an estimated population of over 2.1 million residents.
1	Since the 17th century, Paris has been one of the world's major centres of finance, diplomacy, commerce, fashion, gastronomy, science, and the arts.
2	The city is situated on the Seine river in northern France, at the heart of the Île-de-France region.
3	Major world-famous landmarks located in Paris include the Eiffel Tower, the Louvre Museum, Notre-Dame Cathedral, and the Arc de Triomphe.
4	The Eiffel Tower was constructed on the Champ de Mars in Paris for the 1889 Exposition Universelle.

text: The Statue of Liberty is a colossal neoclassical sculpture on Liberty Island in New York Harbor in New York City, United States.
lines:
0	The Statue of Liberty is a colossal neoclassical sculpture on Liberty Island in New York Harbor within New York City, in the United States.
1	The copper statue, a gift from the people of France to the people of the United States, was designed by French sculptor Frédéric Auguste Bartholdi.
2	Its metal framework was built by Gustave Eiffel, the same engineer who designed the Eiffel Tower.
3	The statue was dedicated on October 28, 1886 by United States President Grover Cleveland.
4	The Statue of Liberty is located in the United States, not in Europe.

text: The Taj Mahal is an ivory-white marble mausoleum on the south bank of the Yamuna river in Agra, India.
lines:
0	The Taj Mahal is an ivory-white marble mausoleum on the right bank of the river Yamuna in Agra, Uttar Pradesh, India.
1	It was commissioned in 1631 by the fifth Mughal emperor, Shah Jahan, to house the tomb of his favourite wife, Mumtaz Mahal.
2	The tomb is the centrepiece of a 17-hectare complex, which includes a mosque and a guest house.
3	The Taj Mahal was designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983 for being 'the jewel of Muslim art in India'.
4	It is located in the city of Agra in northern India.

text: The Colosseum is an elliptical amphitheatre in the centre of the city of Rome, Italy.
lines:
0	The Colosseum is an elliptical amphitheatre in the centre of the city of Rome, Italy, just east of the Roman Forum.
1	It is the largest ancient amphitheatre ever built, and is still the largest standing amphitheatre in the world today.
2	Construction began under the emperor Vespasian in 72 AD and was completed in 80 AD under his successor and heir, Titus.
3	The Colosseum could hold an estimated 50,000 to 80,000 spectators at various points in its history.
4	It is situated entirely within Rome, Italy.

text: Alan Mathison Turing was an English mathematician, computer scientist, logician and cryptanalyst.
lines:
0	Alan Mathison Turing (23 June 1912 - 7 June 1954) was an English mathematician, computer scientist, logician, cryptanalyst, philosopher, and theoretical biologist.
1	Turing was highly influential in the development of theoretical computer science, providing a formalisation of the concepts of algorithm and computation with the Turing machine.
2	He is widely considered to be the father of theoretical computer science and artificial intelligence.
3	During the Second World War, Turing was a leading participant in war-time codebreaking at Bletchley Park.
4	He played a pivotal role in cracking intercepted coded messages including the German Enigma machine.
5	Turing was prosecuted in 1952 for homosexual acts; the Labouchere Amendment had made male homosexual activity illegal in the United Kingdom.
6	He died on 7 June 1954 from cyanide poisoning.

text: Apollo 11 was the American spaceflight that first landed humans on the Moon.
lines:
0	Apollo 11 was the American spaceflight that first landed humans on the Moon.
1	Commander Neil Armstrong and lunar module pilot Buzz Aldrin landed the Apollo Lunar Module Eagle on July 20, 1969.
2	Armstrong became the first person to step onto the lunar surface six hours and 39 minutes later on July 21.
3	Aldrin joined him 19 minutes later, and they spent about two and a quarter hours together exploring the site.
4	Command module pilot Michael Collins flew the command module Columbia alone in lunar orbit.
5	Apollo 11 effectively proved US victory in the Space Race with the Soviet Union.

text: Albert Einstein was a German-born theoretical physicist.
lines:
0	Albert Einstein (14 March 1879 - 18 April 1955) was a German-born theoretical physicist who is widely held to be one of the greatest and most influential scientists of all time.
1	Best known for developing the theory of relativity, Einstein also made important contributions to quantum mechanics.
2	His mass-energy equivalence formula E = mc2 has been called 'the world's most famous equation'.
3	He received the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics for his services to theoretical physics, and especially for his discovery of the law of the photoelectric effect.
4	Einstein settled in the United States in 1933 and became an American citizen in 1940.

text: Mount Everest is Earth's highest mountain above sea level.
lines:
0	Mount Everest is Earth's highest mountain above sea level, located in the Mahalangur Himal sub-range of the Himalayas.
1	The China-Nepal border runs across its summit point.
2	Its elevation of 8,848.86 m was most recently established in 2020 by the Chinese and Nepali authorities.
3	Mount Everest attracts many climbers, including highly experienced mountaineers.
4	The first confirmed ascent was achieved by Sir Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay on 29 May 1953.

text: The Godfather is a 1972 American crime film directed by Francis Ford Coppola.
lines:
0	The Godfather is a 1972 American crime film directed by Francis Ford Coppola, who co-wrote the screenplay with Mario Puzo.
1	It is based on Puzo's best-selling 1969 novel of the same title.
2	The film stars Marlon Brando, Al Pacino, James Caan, Richard Castellano, Robert Duvall, Sterling Hayden, John Marley, Richard Conte, and Diane Keaton.
3	It is the first installment in The Godfather trilogy, chronicling the Corleone family under patriarch Vito Corleone.
4	At the 45th Academy Awards, the film won Best Picture, Best Actor for Marlon Brando, and Best Adapted Screenplay.

text: Photosynthesis is a biological process used by plants and other organisms to convert light energy into chemical energy.
lines:
0	Photosynthesis is a biological process used by plants and other organisms to convert light energy into chemical energy.
1	This chemical energy is stored in carbohydrate molecules, such as sugars, which are synthesized from carbon dioxide and water.
2	In most cases, oxygen is also released as a waste product.
3	Most plants, algae, and cyanobacteria perform photosynthesis; such organisms are called photoautotrophs.
4	Photosynthesis is largely responsible for producing and maintaining the oxygen content of the Earth's atmosphere.

text: The Roman Empire was the post-Republican period of ancient Rome.
lines:
0	The Roman Empire was the post-Republican period of ancient Rome.
1	As a polity, it included large territorial holdings around the Mediterranean Sea in Europe, North Africa, and Western Asia, ruled by emperors.
2	The first two centuries of the empire saw a period of unprecedented stability and prosperity known as the Pax Romana.
3	Rome reached its greatest territorial extent under Emperor Trajan in 117 AD.
4	The Western Roman Empire collapsed in 476 AD when Romulus Augustulus was deposed by the Germanic warlord Odoacer.

text: Marie Curie was a Polish and naturalised-French physicist and chemist who conducted pioneering research on radioactivity.
lines:
0	Marie Salomea Skłodowska-Curie (7 November 1867 - 4 July 1934) was a Polish and naturalised-French physicist and chemist.
1	She was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize, the first person to win a Nobel Prize twice, and the only person to win a Nobel Prize in two scientific fields.
2	She won the 1903 Nobel Prize in Physics with her husband Pierre Curie and Henri Becquerel.
3	In 1911, she won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for her discovery of the elements polonium and radium.
4	Curie died in 1934 from aplastic anemia caused by exposure to radiation during her scientific research.

text: Deoxyribonucleic acid is a polymer composed of two polynucleotide chains that coil around each other to form a double helix.
lines:
0	Deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) is a polymer composed of two polynucleotide chains that coil around each other to form a double helix.
1	It carries genetic instructions for the development, functioning, growth and reproduction of all known organisms and many viruses.
2	DNA and ribonucleic acid (RNA) are nucleic acids.
3	The two DNA strands are also known as polynucleotides since they are composed of simpler monomeric units called nucleotides.
4	The double-helix model of DNA structure was first published in the journal Nature by James Watson and Francis Crick in 1953.

text: Nikolaj William Coster-Waldau is a Danish actor, producer and screenwriter.
lines:
0	Nikolaj William Coster-Waldau (born 27 July 1970) is a Danish actor, producer and screenwriter.
1	He graduated from the Danish National School of Performing Arts in Copenhagen in 1993.
2	Coster-Waldau's breakthrough performance in Denmark was the role in the film Nightwatch (1994).
3	He became widely known for his role as Jaime Lannister in the HBO fantasy series Game of Thrones.
4	In 2008, he starred as Detective John Amsterdam in the Fox television series New Amsterdam.
5	He worked with the Fox Broadcasting Company on several productions.

text: Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun and the second-smallest planet in the Solar System.
lines:
0	Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun and the second-smallest planet in the Solar System, being larger than only Mercury.
1	Mars carries the name of the Roman god of war and is often referred to as the 'Red Planet'.
2	The red appearance is caused by iron oxide (rust) on its surface.
3	Mars is a terrestrial planet with a thin atmosphere, having surface features reminiscent of the impact craters of the Moon.
4	Liquid water cannot exist on the surface of Mars due to low atmospheric pressure.

text: Sir Isaac Newton was an English mathematician, physicist, astronomer, alchemist, and author.
lines:
0	Sir Isaac Newton (4 January 1643 - 31 March 1727) was an English polymath active as a mathematician, physicist, astronomer, alchemist, and author.
1	He was a key figure in the Scientific Revolution and the Enlightenment that followed.
2	His pioneering book Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica (Mathematical Principles of Natural Philosophy), first published in 1687, established classical mechanics.
3	Newton formulated the laws of motion and universal gravitation, which formed the dominant scientific viewpoint until relativity.
4	He also built the first practical reflecting telescope and developed infinitesimal calculus.

text: Leonardo di ser Piero da Vinci was an Italian polymath of the High Renaissance.
lines:
0	Leonardo di ser Piero da Vinci (15 April 1452 - 2 May 1519) was an Italian polymath of the High Renaissance.
1	He was active as a painter, draughtsman, engineer, scientist, theorist, sculptor, and architect.
2	Leonardo is widely regarded as one of the greatest painters in history; his Mona Lisa is the most famous portrait ever created.
3	His drawing of the Vitruvian Man is also regarded as an iconic cultural masterpiece.
4	He painted The Last Supper, the most reproduced religious painting of all time.

text: The Great Wall of China is a series of fortifications that were built across the historical northern borders of ancient Chinese states.
lines:
0	The Great Wall of China is a series of fortifications that were built across the historical northern borders of ancient Chinese states and Imperial China.
1	It was constructed as protection against various nomadic groups from the Eurasian Steppe.
2	Several walls were built from as early as the 7th century BC, with selective stretches joined together by Qin Shi Huang, the first emperor of China.
3	Little of the Qin wall remains; the best-known sections were built by the Ming dynasty (1368-1644).
4	Totaling 21,196 km in length, the Great Wall is located in China.

text: The Fox Broadcasting Company is an American commercial broadcast television network.
lines:
0	The Fox Broadcasting Company is an American commercial broadcast television network.
1	It is a flagship property of the Fox Corporation.
2	The network is headquartered at the Fox Studios Lot in Los Angeles, California.
3	Fox has produced numerous popular television programs, including New Amsterdam starring Nikolaj Coster-Waldau.
4	It was launched on October 9, 1986, as a competitor to the Big Three television networks.

text: Neil Alden Armstrong was an American astronaut and aeronautical engineer who became the first person to walk on the Moon in 1969.
lines:
0	Neil Alden Armstrong was an American astronaut and aeronautical engineer who became the first person to walk on the Moon in 1969.
1	He was also a naval aviator, test pilot, and university professor.
2	Armstrong developed his passion for aviation at a young age and earned his student pilot certificate at age 16.
3	On July 20, 1969, Armstrong and Apollo 11 Lunar Module pilot Buzz Aldrin became the first people to land on the Moon.
4	The following day, Armstrong stepped onto the lunar surface and spoke the famous words: "That's one small step for man, one giant leap for mankind."

text: Buzz Aldrin is an American former astronaut, engineer and fighter pilot.
lines:
0	Buzz Aldrin is an American former astronaut, engineer and fighter pilot.
1	He made three spacewalks as pilot of the 1966 Gemini 12 mission.
2	As the Lunar Module pilot on the 1969 Apollo 11 mission, he and Neil Armstrong were the first two people to land on the Moon.
3	Aldrin was the second person to walk on the Moon, stepping onto the lunar surface nineteen minutes after Armstrong.
4	Aldrin was born Edwin Eugene Aldrin Jr. in Glen Ridge, New Jersey.

text: Francis Ford Coppola is an American film director, producer, and screenwriter.
lines:
0	Francis Ford Coppola is an American film director, producer, and screenwriter.
1	He is considered one of the major figures of the New Hollywood filmmaking movement of the 1960s and 1970s.
2	Coppola directed The Godfather in 1972, which revolutionized filmmaking and won three Academy Awards.
3	His accolades include five Academy Awards, six Golden Globe Awards, and two Palmes d'Or.
4	Coppola attended Hofstra University and later studied filmmaking at UCLA.

text: The Giza pyramid complex is the site on the Giza Plateau in Greater Cairo, Egypt.
lines:
0	The Giza pyramid complex, also called the Giza necropolis, is the site on the Giza Plateau in Greater Cairo, Egypt.
1	It includes the Great Pyramid of Giza, the Pyramid of Khafre, and the Pyramid of Menkaure.
2	The Great Pyramid of Giza was built in the 26th century BC for Pharaoh Khufu.
3	It is the oldest of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World, and the only one to remain largely intact.
4	The pyramids are located on the western bank of the Nile River in Egypt.

text: Egypt is a transcontinental country spanning the northeast corner of Africa and southwest corner of Asia.
lines:
0	Egypt is a transcontinental country spanning the northeast corner of Africa and southwest corner of Asia via the Sinai Peninsula.
1	It is bordered by the Mediterranean Sea to the north and the Red Sea to the east.
2	Cairo is the capital and largest city of Egypt.
3	The Great Pyramids of Giza and the Great Sphinx are famous ancient Egyptian monuments located near Cairo.
4	The official language of Egypt is Modern Standard Arabic.

text: Tokyo is the capital and most populous prefecture of Japan.
lines:
0	Tokyo is the capital and most populous prefecture of Japan.
1	Located at the head of Tokyo Bay, the prefecture forms part of the Kantō region on the central Pacific coast of Japan's main island of Honshu.
2	Tokyo is the political and economic center of Japan, as well as the seat of the Emperor of Japan and the national government.
3	The Greater Tokyo Area is the most populous metropolitan area in the world, with over 37 million residents.
4	Notable landmarks include the Tokyo Skytree, Tokyo Tower, and the historic Sensō-ji temple.

text: Japan is an island country in East Asia situated in the northwest Pacific Ocean.
lines:
0	Japan is an island country in East Asia situated in the northwest Pacific Ocean.
1	It borders the Sea of Japan to the west and extends from the Sea of Okhotsk in the north toward the East China Sea and Taiwan in the south.
2	Japan is an archipelago of over 14,000 islands, with the five main islands being Hokkaido, Honshu, Shikoku, Kyushu, and Okinawa.
3	The capital and largest city of Japan is Tokyo.
4	Mount Fuji is the highest mountain in Japan, rising to 3,776 meters.

text: William Shakespeare was an English playwright, poet and actor.
lines:
0	William Shakespeare was an English playwright, poet and actor.
1	He is widely regarded as the greatest writer in the English language and the world's pre-eminent dramatist.
2	His extant works include approximately 39 plays, 154 sonnets, and three long narrative poems.
3	His famous plays include Hamlet, Romeo and Juliet, Othello, King Lear, and Macbeth.
4	Shakespeare was born and raised in Stratford-upon-Avon, Warwickshire.

text: The Nile is a major north-flowing river in northeastern Africa.
lines:
0	The Nile is a major north-flowing river in northeastern Africa.
1	It flows into the Mediterranean Sea and is the longest river in Africa.
2	The Nile has historically been considered the longest river in the world, measuring approximately 6,650 kilometers.
3	The drainage basin of the Nile encompasses eleven countries, including Egypt, Sudan, South Sudan, Ethiopia, and Uganda.
4	The Nile is the primary water source of Egypt and Sudan, sustaining agriculture and civilization along its valley.

text: World War II was a global conflict that lasted from 1939 to 1945.
lines:
0	World War II was a global conflict that lasted from 1939 to 1945.
1	The vast majority of the world's countries formed two opposing military alliances: the Allies and the Axis powers.
2	Major Axis powers included Nazi Germany, the Kingdom of Italy, and the Empire of Japan.
3	Major Allied powers included the United Kingdom, the Soviet Union, the United States, and China.
4	World War II resulted in an estimated 70 to 85 million fatalities, making it the deadliest conflict in human history.

text: Alexander III of Macedon was a king of the ancient Greek kingdom of Macedon.
lines:
0	Alexander III of Macedon, commonly known as Alexander the Great, was a king of the ancient Greek kingdom of Macedon.
1	He succeeded his father Philip II to the throne in 336 BC at the age of 20.
2	By the age of thirty, he had created one of the largest empires in history, stretching from Greece to northwestern India.
3	He was undefeated in battle and is widely considered one of history's most successful military commanders.
4	He was tutored by the philosopher Aristotle until the age of 16.

text: Charles Robert Darwin was an English naturalist, geologist and biologist.
lines:
0	Charles Robert Darwin was an English naturalist, geologist and biologist.
1	He is best known for his contributions to evolutionary biology.
2	His proposition that all species of life have descended from common ancestors is now widely accepted and considered a fundamental concept in science.
3	In 1859, Darwin published his theory of evolution with compelling evidence in his landmark book On the Origin of Species.
4	Darwin formulated his ideas while conducting fieldwork on HMS Beagle, notably at the Galápagos Islands.

text: Ludwig van Beethoven was a German composer and pianist.
lines:
0	Ludwig van Beethoven was a German composer and pianist.
1	He is one of the most admired figures in the history of Western music; his works rank amongst the most performed of the classical music repertoire.
2	Beethoven's works span the transition from the classical period to the romantic era in classical music.
3	His best-known compositions include nine symphonies, five piano concertos, one violin concerto, and 32 piano sonatas.
4	Beethoven began losing his hearing in his late twenties and was almost completely deaf by 1814.

text: The United States of America is a country primarily located in North America.
lines:
0	The United States of America is a country primarily located in North America.
1	It consists of 50 states, a federal district, five major unincorporated territories, and minor outlying islands.
2	The national capital of the United States is Washington, D.C., and its most populous city is New York City.
3	The United States declared its independence from Great Britain on July 4, 1776.
4	The United States is a federal republic and a representative democracy with three distinct branches of government.
